knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes two-sample confidence intervals in the Normal / binomial / Poisson settings?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the independent two-sample contrast claim.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Two-sample CIs target contrasts under independent sampling. Equal n does not create pairing, and pooling into one sample erases the contrast.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: CI for a contrast between two independent samples (Normal or Normal-approx discrete).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating equal-n independent samples as paired, or pooling away the contrast.

choices.label: Form a CI for a contrast between two independent samples (for example a difference of means or of probabilities/means), using Normal models or Normal approximations as appropriate.
If two samples have equal size, they may be analysed as paired data even when observations are not matched.
Two-sample intervals always pool the observations into one sample and then use a one-sample CI for the grand mean.
Two-sample CIs require dependent observations within pairs; independent groups are handled only by prediction intervals.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Independent samples of claim amounts from portfolio A and portfolio B (Normal model). Which statement is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Independent two-sample CIs need independent groups and usually target a difference of means. Pairing is a different design; equal n is not enough to justify paired analysis.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Target μ_A − μ_B under independent samples; refuse paired-as-equal-n.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Applying independent two-sample formulas to paired rows (or the reverse) because n₁=n₂.

choices.label: A two-sample CI typically targets μ_A − μ_B under independent samples from the two groups. Paired before/after rows are not the same design: equal sample sizes do not turn matched pairs into an independent two-sample problem.
If n_A = n_B, analyse the data as paired differences even when there is no natural matching between A and B units.
Independence between samples is optional; the two-sample mean difference CI is valid for any dependence structure.
The two-sample CI targets μ_A / μ_B only, never a difference, when the model is Normal.

worked_example.title: 95% CI for difference of two mean claim costs
worked_example.problem_statement: Independent samples from portfolios A and B (Normal, known variances): n_A = 40, x̄_A = £8,200, σ_A = £1,200; n_B = 45, x̄_B = £7,600, σ_B = £1,100. Construct a 95% CI for μ_A − μ_B.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Write SE = √(σ_A²/n_A + σ_B²/n_B) before the interval.

steps.label: Point estimate of the difference
steps.explanation: The natural centre for μ_A − μ_B is the difference of sample means.

steps.label: SE of the difference
steps.explanation: Independence adds the variances of the two sample means.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Pooling into √(σ²(1/n_A+1/n_B)) with a single σ, or subtracting SEs instead of adding variances under the square root.
